facts.claim: Older individuals tend to be more susceptible to dark patterns.

facts.claim: Decision architecture, not price, drove consumer purchasing decisions.
facts.quote: Decision architecture, not price, drove consumer purchasing decisions.

facts.claim: In a study of 195 adult volunteers aged 19 to 53, participants were significantly more likely to select products with dark patterns.
facts.quote: Results indicated that participants were significantly more likely to select products with dark patterns.

facts.claim: The use of limited-time message dark pattern was significantly more effective than other dark patterns in inducing consumption.
facts.quote: The use of limited-time message dark pattern was significantly more effective than other dark patterns in inducing consumption.

facts.claim: Firms' proprietary A-B testing has revealed dark patterns to be profit maximizing.
facts.quote: Dark patterns are presumably proliferating because firms’ proprietary A-B testing has revealed them to be profit maximizing.

facts.claim: Analyzing ~53K product pages from ~11K shopping websites, researchers discovered 1,818 dark pattern instances, representing 15 types and 7 broader categories.
facts.quote: Analyzing ~53K product pages from ~11K shopping websites, we discover 1,818 dark pattern instances, together representing 15 types and 7 broader categories.

research.angle: Dark patterns are profit-maximizing design choices that successfully manipulate consumers into making unintended purchases, with limited-time messages being particularly effective.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that dark patterns are widespread and effective at influencing consumer behavior to maximize profit.
research.caveat: The study on awareness interventions found no clear evidence that video- or activity-based methods effectively reduce the impact of dark patterns.
